title: Doodle Hoot
description: One player draws while everyone else guesses: type it, call it out, or use letter tiles for little ones. Host it live for your family or friends: everyone joins with a code on their own phone, tablet or computer, wherever they are, and takes turns to draw. Or play on your own: guess the doodles Pip the owl draws, or pass one device round and take turns. Words in 13 languages, from Easy to Tricky. No chat: a guess only ever goes to the game.
notes: In Crossword's look (the classroom dashboard's widgets, docs/decisions.md "Doodle Hoot in Crossword's look"): a dotted mint board behind everything, cream widget cards with a group colour on the top edge and an icon chip (the setup card with Pip in its chip; Pens, Your guess or the tiles, Guesses and Scores beside the board; the word cards, covers, lobby and end screen as one card on the board; Who guessed it?; the kit's results card restyled with a trophy chip), the dark Now bar for the round, who is drawing, the word or blanks and the clock (green in dark mode, as Crossword's), pill buttons, Bricolage Grotesque from Google Fonts, light and dark from BRB.theme through the kit (else the device). The Oomba Kit (pinned 1.1.6 plus the art-animals, dress and live packs) stays underneath as plumbing: the game loop, Pip and the players' figures, sounds, the results card and BRB.gameOver, settings and reduced motion, and Oomba Live. The drawing board is a fixed 1000 x 750 grid (4:3) drawn on paper white in both themes (a white card on the board), with 12 colours, 4 sizes, an eraser, undo and clear, for touch, pen and mouse (the primary pointer only). The rules, the tray builder, the guess check, the hints and the points are window.DoodleCore (pure, between /* doodle-core:begin */ and /* doodle-core:end */); the reviewed word list is window.DoodleWords (about 160 things to draw over 3 levels in 12 word lists plus en-GB words, between /* doodle-words:begin */ and /* doodle-words:end */); server/live/doodle-core.js runs the same blocks for Oomba Live. Guessing is typed by default (DoodleCore.judge: case, accents, spaces, hyphens, articles, plurals and the other English spelling don't matter; a letter or two off is 'So close!'), or letter tiles (the easier choice): a tile is one grapheme (spaces are never tiles); the tray is the answer's tiles plus decoys (never a letter of the answer; an Easy tray never puts a letter next to its accent twin); a tile guess is tray positions. On its own: a setup card (Guess Pip's doodles or Pass and play; Easy, Medium or Tricky words; typing or letter tiles; 2-6 players for pass and play), remembered in BRB.storage key 'doodle-hoot-v1' (choices and the best practice score only, never a drawing). Guess Pip's doodles: 8 of Pip's own doodles (window.DoodleArt) drawn stroke by stroke, 45 s each, hints over time, points 50-100 by speed, the kit results card with stars; it submits BRB.gameOver({won, score}). Pass and play: each player draws once (60 s) while the others watch and call out guesses (the word stays covered; 'Someone said it!' and who ends the turn), or after Done the others guess it together and tap who got it; nothing is submitted (a shared screen). Oomba Live (built-in mode 'doodle', docs/live-protocol.md "Doodle Hoot Live"): the same file draws the live view when Oomba.live.active: the server runs the turns, sends the drawer 3 words (ch) and each guesser the turn (tray), relays checked strokes (ln, un, cl) from memory only, checks every guess for the whole drawing (gs -> gr: typed as code points, compared and forgotten, or tray positions) and sends hints (hd, hn); the drawer or the host can award a guess said out loud (aw); the drawer and the projector see the guesses so far (fd: a word of the list, or only 'something else'); the projector shows the drawing, blank slots, the guesses and who got it (no scores and no podium: each phone shows its own points; the end shows everyone who played); each player can hide a drawing for themselves (hide). The one text box is the guess box, whose text goes to the server only; no chat. window.__brbTest: state/setup/start({mode, lvl, players, guess})/pick(i)/draw(points)/ready/done/tap(i)/spell(word)/type(word)/said/who(k)/skipAnimations (solo); state/pick/draw/tap/spell/type/said/who/undo/clear/hide (live).
